newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Active Hansa Bank boosts Estonian bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: Active Hansa Bank boosts Estonian bourse trade.

text.p: Trade in leading bank Hansa Bank buoyed an otherwise quiet Estonian stock market on Monday with some dealers confident its shares have further to go.
Hansa Bank turned over 4.8 million kroons out of overall market volume of 5.8 million kroons. The Tallinn stock exchange index was barely moved, slipping 0.01 percent to 97.98.
Hansa Bank shares closed slightly higher at 94.47 kroons, versus 94.10 kroons on Friday.
"Hansa Bank shares are certainly the most attractive securities on the bourse," said Charline Viikberg, a dealer with Savings Bank.
He said Hansa Bank's shares could easily rise as far 100 kroons.
Hansa Bank, which also has a quote in Helsinki, is one of the most liquid stocks in Estonia and has attracted consistent investor interest.
Other stocks on the official list were quiet. Union Bank was the second most active on trade of just over 500,000 kroons. It closed at 23 kroons versus 23.10.
On the secondary free market list, the Tallinna Kaubamaja department store was the most active at just over 570,000 kroons amid overall activity of 1.5 million kroons.
